short: Phone-model decoder (M06) is the EMG recognizer moved to ECoG: standard. 25% WER uses per-phrase dictionaries holding the spoken words (M07); the time-shift null (M12) is sound.
position: Brain-to-Text [@herff2015] changes the decoder (M06): Gaussian phone models on ECoG broadband gamma, joined to a dictionary and a bigram model by Viterbi search. This is standard: the chain is that of continuous EMG recognizers co-authored by Schultz [@jou2006; @schultz2010], uncited by the paper (References), moved to a new signal; the Abstract's priority claim is scoped to ECoG. The lexicon (M07) is the weak point: each test phrase gets a dictionary containing its spoken words (§2.11), and bigrams come from the read texts with no stated exclusion of the test phrase (§2.10), whereas the EMG prior kept test sentences out of its language model [@jou2006]. The 25% WER is a closed-set figure on overt read speech, not comparable with the 25% median WER of [later] ECoG work on attempted speech in paralysis over a 1,024-word set [@metzger2023]. The evaluation (M12) is standard; its time-shifted null, keeping dictionary and language model, is the strongest design choice. Scaling beyond dictionaries holding the spoken words, and beyond the session, is unsupported.
